summary: The original inspector-navigation focus-loss defect is corrected, and no supported defect was found in the rapid selection/filter URL composition. One limited residual focus-request cancellation issue remains for pointer blur to non-focusable content.
coverage: Verified all six review-fix-source.json SHA256 pins before and after this bounded correction pass; preserved the original review artifacts.

Inspected ObservatoryPage navigationFocus identity/lifetime, navigation ref focus restoration, parent/sibling controls, and enabled boundary fallback; traced cached, loading, error and threat inspector headers.
Confirmed InspectorSelection remains keyed by workspace/node and draft/dialog lifetime boundaries are unchanged. Inspected modal focus capture/restoration and existing keyboard isolation tests.

Traced immediate selectNode UI updates, filter/selection writes composed from current window.location.search, stale router-param effect suppression, framework switching, reset view and canvas key selection.
Read the added repeated sibling/parent focus browser test and corrected coarse-pointer phone fixture. Tests were inspected but not executed.

findings.mechanism: After an inspector navigation restores focus, the request remains live for later header swaps. Clicking non-focusable content outside the navigation blurs its button with relatedTarget null, which the onBlurCapture guard ignores. A subsequent Observatory rerender, such as a scene hover or assessment refresh, receives a newly created navigation ref callback; with activeElement now body, it restores the old navigation focus even though the user already clicked elsewhere. This does not overwrite a focused form or dialog, but does produce an unsolicited keyboard-focus jump.
findings.evidence: The focus request set at 377 is not consumed by restoration at 382-386. Identity cleanup at 282-285 only clears it if workspace or selectedId changes. The blur handler at 388-389 requires relatedTarget instanceof Node, excluding normal blur to non-focusable content. restoreNavigationFocus is recreated on every page render and accepts body focus, while onHover at 341-345 updates page/global state. This is a source-supported edge case; no browser reproduction was executed in this review.
findings.recommendation: Cancel pending navigation restoration on an intentional pointer interaction outside the navigation, including non-focusable targets, while retaining it across keyed/loading header replacement. Keep the current active-element and workspace/node guards.

limitations: This was a bounded follow-up to the original review, with the lead-provided correction rationale visible; it is not a new independent review of the whole feature.
No browsers, builds, tests or live data were executed. Runtime focus, exact loading timing and rapid input ordering remain owned by the separate integration lane.
The residual null-relatedTarget pointer-blur finding is source-derived and limited to focus returning from body; active form/dialog focus is protected by the current guard.
